og.title: Snugtone, a music player in Rust
og.description: For your own library: fast, MIT-licensed, and it never touches your files.

pullQuote.label: Why
pullQuote.text: foobar2000 felt very dated to me, and it had too much going on. I wanted something simpler and faster that still read the formats everyone uses. And to learn Rust along the way.

items.title: It plays.
items.text: FLAC, MP3, Opus, WAV, AAC, ALAC, Vorbis and AIFF, gapless between tracks. Every album at the same volume: it measures loudness itself (EBU R128, per album, within 0.04 LU of ffmpeg). A ten-band equalizer that, switched off, doesn't touch a single bit. And if your headphones switch off mid-song, it moves to another output and keeps playing from the same millisecond.

items.title: It's fast with a big library.
text: A rescan in 0.48 s, the list on screen in under a second, watched folders and a search box that narrows things down (

items.title: It fixes things without touching your files.
items.text: It checks FLAC and ALAC sample by sample against their MD5, corrects tags in the library rather than in the file, and brings tags from MusicBrainz, showing the comparison field by field before anything changes.

items.title: It's yours to set up.
items.text: Theme, density, columns, audio output and every shortcut, all from within the app, with changes applied instantly; underneath, three plain TOML files. In English and Spanish.

layerStack.title: How it's built
layerStack.lede: The core is pure Rust (audio engine, queue, library, configuration) and doesn't know Tauri exists, so it's tested without opening a window. The Tauri shell provides the window and the real audio output (cpal). The interface is HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework and no build step.

columns.title: Download
columns.text: The Windows installer is on GitHub. It isn't signed, so Windows will warn you with «Windows protected your PC»: click «More info» and then «Run anyway». The code is meant for Linux too, which comes next; macOS and mobile, later. MIT license.
